newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * The parliament's upper and lower chambers resumed debates on the 1997 budget and discussed chapters on ministry expenditures.

The education ministry will need to cut 58,000 jobs to contain the budget. Some 14,000 employees in agriculture -- mainly coming from state-run farms on liquidation and privatisation programmes -- will also lose their jobs.
* Top businessman George Constantin Paunescu was heard by prosecutors on Wednesday as part of investigations into alleged forgery and embezzelment, the head of Romanian Police said.
* The National Unity Party (PUNR) agrees with a government step to control the State Ownership Fund, but said the measure should have been approved by parliament, PUNR leaders said.

They said the party will vote against the 1997 budget currently under debate in parliament, saying all amendments proposed by the PUNR were ignored by ruling coalition MPs. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
